title: Bidirectional Diffusion Bridge Models

problem.claim: Paired image-to-image translation requires modeling translation between coupled image distributions.

gap.claim: Existing diffusion bridge methods are unidirectional, requiring separate models for forward and reverse translation, which doubles computational cost and restricts practicality.

contributions.claim: BDBM enables bidirectional translation between two coupled distributions using a single network.
BDBM uses the Chapman-Kolmogorov Equation for bridges to model distribution shifts in both directions by interchanging initial and target timesteps.
For Gaussian marginal distributions given endpoints, BDBM has analytical transition kernels in both directions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that BDBM enables bidirectional translation with minimal additional cost on high-resolution image-to-image translation tasks.
The authors report that BDBM outperforms state-of-the-art bridge models in their experiments.
The authors report that source code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion bridges have shown potential for paired image-to-image translation.
Existing methods are unidirectional and require separate forward and reverse models, increasing computational cost and limiting practicality.
BDBM uses one network for bidirectional translation and exploits Chapman-Kolmogorov bridge structure across interchangeable timesteps.
Gaussian endpoint-conditioned marginals yield analytical transition kernels for both directions.
The authors connect BDBM to existing bridge methods and report high-resolution experiments with minimal additional cost and improved performance over state-of-the-art bridge models.

source_observation.claim: A single network can support translation in both directions when the bridge formulation permits interchangeability of initial and target timesteps.

interpretation.claim: Bidirectional modeling may reduce duplicated model capacity and computational cost.

application.claim: For paired distribution-translation systems, investigate shared bidirectional parameterizations before deploying separate directional models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this sharing is effective beyond the reported image-to-image translation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative metrics, or the magnitude of the reported performance improvements.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or resource requirements for the single-network model.
